Lessons.Title: Multi-step Measurement Problems
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will apply what you learned about metric units of measurement and multiplicative comparison to solve multi-step problems.
In the preceding lessons, you learned about the relationship between centimeters and meters, grams and kilograms, and liters and milliliters.
Core relationship: Multi-step measurement conversions. Convert distances or capacities to a common unit first, then operate.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Notice and Wonder: Distances Traveled	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Long Hikes, Short Hikes	 (20 minutes); Activity 2:  Big Bottles, Little Bottles	 (15 minutes); Cool-down:  Hydration Here and There	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: Find total distance of 2 km and 750 m in meters.
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): A trip uses 1 km 200 m then 900 m; total meters?
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

KeyConcepts.Title: Multi-step measurement conversions
KeyConcepts.Rule: Convert distances or capacities to a common unit first, then operate.
KeyConcepts.Example: Find total distance of 2 km and 750 m in meters.

WorkedExamples.Title: Source-aligned mathematical model
WorkedExamples.Question: Find total distance of 2 km and 750 m in meters.
WorkedExamples.Method: Convert distances or capacities to a common unit first, then operate.
Steps: Identify all quantities and common units.
Confirm 2,750 by the inverse or a visual model.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Adding meter values directly to kilometer values.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Convert distances or capacities to a common unit first, then operate.

SummaryPoints: Independently authored first-party Cool-down; not original publisher item.
